title: Cooperation or competition: which helps more?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Each helps in its place; many wins use both

explain.say: Think of a football team. Inside the team, players pass to each other. Against the other team, they try to win. So is football about cooperation or competition? Both! Look at the board: two ways humans get things done, side by side.

draw.text: Cooperation or competition: which helps more?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Each helps in its place; many wins use both

explain.say: See the left side, cooperation? Cooperation means working together towards the same goal, sharing ideas and effort. It built villages, bridges and the International Space Station, where 15 countries work together. It builds trust. When do you cooperate at home?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Each helps in its place; many wins use both

explain.say: Now look at the right side, competition. Competition means trying to do better than others. It can push you to practise, improve and invent; shops compete with better prices, athletes with faster times. It can also lead to cheating or hurt feelings. When does competition help you try harder?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Each helps in its place; many wins use both

explain.say: Look at the bottom of each side. Both have a downside: cooperation can let someone hide and do nothing, and competition can make people unkind. Economists and psychologists debate how much of each works best, and the answer depends on the task. Which do you enjoy more?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Each helps in its place; many wins use both

explain.say: Often the best results mix both: teams cooperate inside and compete outside, like Olympic relay teams. Great thinking! Wow fact: scientists racing to make COVID-19 vaccines both competed and shared data, and the first vaccines were ready in under a year.

faq.a: Neither is always better. Cooperation is great for big shared jobs and builds trust; competition pushes people to improve and invent. Many of the best results combine both, like teams that cooperate inside and compete with rivals.
asks: Which is better, cooperation or competition?

faq.a: Cooperation means people working together towards a shared goal, sharing effort, ideas and rewards. Humans cooperate with strangers on a huge scale, more than almost any other animal.

Competition means trying to win or do better than others, for a prize, a place, customers or a record. Healthy competition pushes people to improve; unhealthy competition can lead to cheating or unkindness.

faq.q: What are the downsides of cooperation and competition?
faq.a: In cooperation, some people may do less and let others work, which is called free riding. In competition, people may cheat, give up, or treat rivals badly.

faq.q: Can cooperation and competition work together?
faq.a: Yes. Sports teams, businesses and scientists often cooperate within their group while competing with others, and even rivals sometimes share knowledge for a bigger goal.
asks: Can you compete and cooperate at once?
Examples of cooperation and competition together

facts: The International Space Station is run by the space agencies of the USA, Russia, Japan, Canada and 11 European countries.
The first COVID-19 vaccines were authorised in December 2020, less than a year after the virus's genetic code was shared publicly in January 2020.

quiz.say: A class builds one big model volcano together. Is that cooperation or competition?
quiz.why: Everyone works towards one shared goal, which is cooperation.

wrong.1: Nobody is trying to beat anyone else.
wrong.2: Working together on a shared goal is a clear case of cooperation.

quiz.say: What is one risk of too much competition?
quiz.show: A risk of too much competition is…

options.show: People may cheat or be unkind
options.say: People may cheat or be unkind

quiz.why: When winning matters too much, some people cheat or treat rivals badly.

wrong.0: Sharing is more a feature of cooperation.
wrong.2: Competition usually makes people try harder, not lazier.
